newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Changan Auto sees 14 pct rise in '97 net.
newsitem.headline: Changan Auto sees 14 pct rise in '97 net.

text.p: China's Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd expects to register net profits of 231.9 million yuan in 1997, up 14.3 percent from 1996, a company official said.
The forecast net profits, based on international accounting standards, compare with net profits of 202.83 million yuan in 1996 and 220.16 million in 1995.
Profits will be fuelled by an expected production increase to 80,000 cars in 1997 from 70,400 cars in 1996, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

Turnover is expected to reach 2.92 billion yuan in 1997 against 2.63 billion in 1996 based on Chinese accounting standards, the company said in an A share prospectus published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Tuesday.

The car maker said in the prospectus it would offer 120 million domestic currency A shares in Shenzhen on Wednesday at 6.36 yuan each, giving an offer price/earnings ratio of 15 times based on net profits averaged over the past three years.
The shares carry a 23.56 times P/E based on forecast 1997 net earnings per share of 0.27 yuan on a fully diluted basis under Chinese standards, the company said.
The company said 37 million of the A shares would be issued as staff shares.
Neither the prospectus nor the official gave the expected 1997 earnings per share based on international standards.
Changan's B shares were trading at HK$4.46, up 2.29 percent, late on Wednesday afternoon.
Changan has appointed China Guotai Securities Co Ltd as the listing sponsor. The company plans to use the proceeds from the issue to boost production.
After the A share offer, the company will have a total of 876.2 million shares, consisting of 506.2 million institutional shares, 250 million B shares and 120 million A shares.
